# dsh-remote-gpu
A DSH plugin that shows **live GPU utilization of the server `dsh-remote` is connected to**.

It piggybacks on `dsh-remote`: the host half calls dsh-remote's own `rw_exec` tool
through the host

`tools` service, so no second SSH connection, no duplicated
credential handling, and no extra depend

s` service, so no second SSH connection, no duplicated
credential handling, and no extra dependency.
## What you get
| Seat | What it shows |
| Conversation header chip | `空闲 {idle}/{total}` — **only how many remote GPUs are free** (colour-co
ded: green = all free, amber = some free, red = none). Click it to open the panel for the details. T

he tooltip also lists the users currently on the GPU box (`占用 <user>×<n>`). |
| Right sidebar tab `远
程显卡` | Every GPU of the remote host in detail: name, utilization %, memory used/total, temperature,
**the user who owns the task running on it** (`占用 <user>×<n>`), a `空闲` tag on the free cards, plus a

sparkline of recent samples. |
| Settings → `远程显卡` | Probe status, remote host, backend, idle count
, refresh interval, the exact probe command, a "refresh now" button, the per-GPU process list (user

· command · pid · memory) and an "active users" summary. |
| Host tool `remote_gpu` | The same snaps
hot as text, so the agent can read it directly. |
## What counts as a free GPU
A card is *idle* when it is barely drawing power **and** barely holding memory:

- utilization `< idleUtilPercent` (default **10 %**), and
- memory used `< idleMemoryPercent` (defau
lt **5 %**) of the card.

Both must hold: a model that is loaded but idle still owns its VRAM, so that
card is not free for a

new job. The host computes the verdict and ships it
with every sample, so the chip, the panel and th

e `remote_gpu` tool always
agree on the same number.

`lib/gpu-parse.js` maps the GPU UUIDs to indices and the PIDs to their owner
(`user` + command), so

each GPU ends up with `processes[]` and a per-GPU
`users[]` summary. On ROCm / gpustat servers the p

rocess list stays empty —
those tools do not expose per-process GPU ownership.
## Motion
Every reading eases into place instead of snapping:

- one shared `requestAnimationFrame` loop drives all tweens, so a panel with
many GPUs still costs a

single frame callback;
- utilization, memory and temperature glide to their new value over ~520 ms

(`TWEEN_MS` in `client.js`);
- the utilization and memory bars, the sparkline line and the chip dot

slow breathing dot, a GPU card fades in when it
appears, and the loading state uses a shimmer instea

d of static text;
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` switches every animation off.
## How the probe works

The host runs one POSIX shell line on the remote machine. It picks the first
available backend and w
raps every part in `==DSHGPU …==` markers:
| Section | Content |

| `host` | `hostname` of the remote machine |
| `backend` | `nvidia-smi`, `rocm-smi`, `gpustat` or `

none` |
| `gpus` | one CSV row per GPU (`index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total`) |
| `

temp` | GPU temperature (NVIDIA only) |
| `uuid` | GPU index → UUID (NVIDIA only, links processes to

GPUs) |
| `procs` | running compute apps: `pid,gpu_uuid,used_memory` (NVIDIA only) |
| `ps` | owner
of each PID: `pid,user,command` (NVIDIA only) |
`lib/gpu-parse.js` parses those sections into the snapshot the UI renders.

Requirements on the remote server: `nvidia-smi` (or `rocm-smi` / `gpustat`) on `PATH`,
and a dsh-rem

ote **active remote workspace** (the probe uses the machine dsh-remote is
currently connected to).

il the next DSH restart and then
silently disappears — the symptom is a vanished chip and a "removed

tool" notice
in the session.

## Layout

One card is ~79 px tall (compact paddings, a single-line footer, a 5 px
utilization bar and a 3 px m

emory bar), so a full node fits into the right
sidebar without scrolling; the panel scrolls when the
re are more GPUs than fit.
